requirements.title: Storage sequences have counted storage units whose sizes come from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV
requirements.source: S19.5.3.2 p1, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF559.
requirements.definition: A storage sequence is a sequence of character, numeric, file, or unspecified storage units; its size is its number of storage units, and the numeric, character, and file storage-unit sizes are related to the ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants.

pending.storage-sequence-counted-units: Use a default integer pair in COMMON as two one-unit numeric objects, write distinct sentinels 101 and 202 through a two-element view, and assert a matching two-object view observes both values in order.
pending.storage-unit-kinds: Use separate plans for default integer, default character length three, and stream file POS inquiry catalogues; assert only the named numeric, character, and file-storage relations, not byte addresses.
pending.iso-fortran-env-storage-size-relation: Initialize integer sentinels to -777 and assert STORAGE_SIZE(0)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, STORAGE_SIZE(0.0)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, STORAGE_SIZE(.true.)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, and STORAGE_SIZE("abc")==3*CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE; do not hard-code the constants.

requirements.title: Default intrinsic scalar storage-unit counts are exact
requirements.definition: In a storage association context, default integer, real, and logical nonpointer scalars occupy one numeric storage unit; double precision real and default complex occupy two contiguous numeric storage units; default character length len occupies len contiguous character storage units.

pending.default-integer-real-logical-one-numeric: Initialize integer result sentinels to -777 and assert STORAGE_SIZE(0)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, STORAGE_SIZE(0.0)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, and STORAGE_SIZE(.false.)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE; mutate one expected relation to 2*NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE.
pending.double-precision-and-default-complex-two: Initialize integer result sentinels to -777 and assert STORAGE_SIZE(0.0D0)==2*NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE and STORAGE_SIZE((1.0,2.0))==2*NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE; mutate one multiplier from 2 to 1.
pending.default-character-length-character-units: Use character(len=5) :: ch="abcde", initialize the observed size to -777, and assert STORAGE_SIZE(ch)==5*CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE; companion len one asserts STORAGE_SIZE("Z")==CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE.

requirements.title: C character kind, other types, and data pointers use distinct unspecified storage units
requirements.definition: The listed nondefault character, other-type, and pointer cases occupy unspecified storage units with distinctions by case, type parameters, rank, and CONTIGUOUS attribute as stated by the storage model.

pending.c-character-kind-unspecified-units: Guard: C_CHAR /= KIND("A"). In the guarded branch declare character(kind=C_CHAR,len=3), initialize a size sentinel to -777, and assert only STORAGE_SIZE(value)>0 plus nonuse of CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE equality as an oracle.
pending.other-type-case-specific-unspecified-uni: Use two distinct derived types with the same scalar integer component and source-review their separate storage association cases; no portable runtime oracle exposes the standard’s unspecified-unit identity apart from same-type value transfer already owned by other facets.
pending.data-pointer-distinct-unspecified-unit: Source-control plan declares integer pointer scalars and rank-one pointers with and without CONTIGUOUS; no conforming EQUIVALENCE/COMMON runtime oracle can inspect the pointer storage unit itself, so fixture evidence must not compare addresses or raw representations.

requirements.title: Sequence type and array storage sequences are component and element sequences
requirements.definition: A nonpointer scalar object of sequence type occupies the sequence of its ultimate components; a nonpointer array occupies contiguous element storage sequences in array element order.

pending.sequence-type-ultimate-component-order: Define a SEQUENCE type with two default integer components, place one object in COMMON, seed both components to -777, write [11,22] through a two-integer associated view, and assert object%first==11 and object%second==22.
pending.array-contiguous-element-order: Place integer a(2,2) in COMMON and read through a four-integer view; assign a(1,1)=11, a(2,1)=22, a(1,2)=33, a(2,2)=44 and assert the view is [11,22,33,44], exposing column-major element order.

requirements.title: Composite storage sequences concatenate constituent units and ignore zero-sized constituents
requirements.source: S19.5.3.2 p3, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF559.
requirements.definition: A sequence of storage sequences forms a storage sequence ordered by each constituent sequence in succession, with zero-sized constituents ignored.

pending.composite-storage-sequence-successive-or: Use a SEQUENCE type containing integer first, integer pair(2), and integer last; seed all four numeric units to -777 through a COMMON integer view, assign component values [1,2,3,4], and assert the view order [1,2,3,4].
pending.zero-sized-constituents-no-payload: Source-review a parameterized SEQUENCE component with zero extent between two integer components and pair it with a COMMON integer view of only the nonzero units; runtime observes the two neighbor sentinels, while the zero-sized constituent contributes no value slot.

requirements.title: Each common block has a storage sequence
requirements.source: S19.5.3.2 p4, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF559.
requirements.definition: Each common block has a storage sequence as specified by the COMMON block rules.

pending.common-block-storage-sequence-exists: Define named COMMON /packet/ a,b in writer and reader scoping units, seed reader-visible values to -777, write a=808 and b=-909 in writer, and assert the reader observes [808,-909] after the call chain.

requirements.title: Storage-unit bit counts are processor-dependent latitude exposed through ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants
requirements.source: S19.5.3.2 p1.storage-unit-size-latitude, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF559.
requirements.definition: The standard relates numeric, character, and file storage-unit sizes to ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants, while the actual bit counts of those storage units are processor-dependent latitude owned by the existing ISO_FORTRAN_ENV catalogues.

pending.storage-unit-bit-counts-processor-depend: No portable oracle hard-codes NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE, CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE, or FILE_STORAGE_SIZE. Future fixtures assert positivity and exact relations such as STORAGE_SIZE(default integer)==NUMERIC_STORAGE_SIZE and STORAGE_SIZE(default character len 3)==3*CHARACTER_STORAGE_SIZE.

accounting.rationale: Storage-sequence definitions, ISO_FORTRAN_ENV relations, and processor-dependent storage-unit size latitude are split.
Defines storage sequences, size as storage-unit count, and storage-unit kinds.
Relates numeric, character, and file storage-unit sizes to ISO_FORTRAN_ENV constants.
Actual storage-unit bit counts are processor-dependent latitude through the named constants.
Eight storage-association-context cases are split into fine units.
Exact one numeric-unit relation for default integer, real and logical scalars.
Defines a guarded unspecified-unit case for nondefault C character kind.
Defines case-specific unspecified units without absolute representation oracle.
Exact array element order storage relation.
Defines composition and zero-sized omission in composite storage sequences.
